title: ASASSN-14ko flares become wider without a later peak, so a self-similar change of the debris fallback time does not explain the 2020-2024 period stall
abstract: Question: the period decrease of the repeating nuclear transient ASASSN-14ko stopped in 2020-2024 (constant X-ray dip clock, 108.44 d) and started again after 2023. Can a steadily decaying orbit with a growing debris fallback time make this stall? Principle: a self-similar change of the fallback time stretches every interval from the stripping pericentre, so the peak must move by at least 2.146 d per day of extra rise width, the decline must scale with the rise, and the X-ray dip must be delayed too. Approach: we used flare-fit posteriors of earlier campaign studies (ASAS-SN g, TESS), NICER/XRT dip samples, and our own fits of the Swift UVW2 flares, and we did errors-in-variables fits, stretch-origin calculations, timing-model comparisons (18 variants) and a 2020-2023 bound. Results: in 2020-2024 the optical peak time does not move with rise width (slope -0.06, 95%: -0.30 to +0.20, 9 flares); the UVW2 slope is 0.64 (0.40-0.80). A stretch is excluded by Delta(-2 lnL) = 27-40. Broad flares spread around a fixed time 4-10 d after the X-ray dip, and their onsets come up to 24 d before the dip. Rise and decline do not scale together (chi2 133/12 optical, 72/5 UV). A delay that grows with flare width or decline never delays the X-ray dips (kappa at most 0.20) and does not make steady decay competitive with the on-off-step clock in 17 of 18 variants. The narrow 2020 and 2023 flares give a stretch factor 0.88 (95% upper 1.25). Conclusion: the 2022-2023 flare broadening is not a fallback-time change, and a self-similar fallback delay does not explain the stall; an orbital change or a non-self-similar delay remains. Limitations: self-similarity is assumed; 9 flares per band; the UV slope rests on two off-state cycles; the 2020-2023 bound depends on the assumed orbit; no data cover flare 41.

display.caption: Optical and UVW2 peak and onset times relative to the constant X-ray clock against rise width. The peaks do not move with width (blue fit); a fallback-time stretch needs the shaded region (slope at least 2.146).
Swift UVW2 flares aligned on the X-ray clock: narrow flares 20, 21, 30, 31 and broad flares 28, 29. Dashed: flare 21 stretched about the dip by the width ratio, the smallest fallback-time stretch.
Delta AIC of steady decay, steady decay plus a fallback delay (kappa >= 0), free-sign width terms and the on-off-step clock in 18 timing variants.
